notes: The upright sheet bears the manuscript page number 42 at the top centre and pale pencil foliation 85 at bottom left. No date is visible. Formula labels include 117, cancelled 118, and revised 119 and 120.

The opening continues an earlier sentence. It describes a quotient extension of (S Pi M_G, Gamma prime), an extension of the groupoid (Pi M_G, Gamma prime) by the integer group with exponent C, and names it in (117). These are statements on the page, not verified results of this reading.

The following paragraph and display are crossed by several long diagonal lines. The words Dans le cas ... on retrouve l'extension ... (tordu). remain readable. The whole region is retained as cancelled; on retrouve is not left uncertain merely because H marked it so.
The cancelled formula has S_C M_G on its left, with no Pi between C and M, and Gamma without an exclamation superscript. Those forms are preserved as written. No mathematical normalization was made.

The cancelled label is visibly written (118 without a closing parenthesis. The draft uses tag* to avoid adding a closing parenthesis, and records the cancellation of the label. There is no written terminal period after the cancelled formula; the nearby dot belongs to the preceding prose sentence.
The next paragraph reads données, not choses. The unnumbered map has Gamma_G with a clear exclamation superscript. No period is visible after its closing parenthesis.

The inserted equivalence G/C is attached immediately after G prime by a curved connector. That connector runs above est, while une is untouched. Est une therefore remains live. Only spécialisation is cancelled, and the inserted replacement reads générisation, with no additional a-l of généralisation.

The final live numeral in 119 has a descending tail and is read as 9; an underlying 8-like figure is represented with doubt. In 120, the apparent revised 20 overlays traces of 19. The revision history is not treated as fully certain, and the underwritten digits retain doubt marks.

The Pi of the map numbered 119 is heavily retraced. Its two uprights and top bar are clear. Small interior strokes do not securely identify a second original symbol, so none has been invented beneath it.

The A after the upper-left S of the square was first written at the main baseline, cancelled, and rewritten as a subscript. Both positions and states are retained. The upper connecting line is labelled gamma; its endpoint has a small downward return but no secure full conventional arrowhead.

The cancelled suffix of the lower-left square object has a visible exclamation upright and dot. Its large angular body remains doubtful under the hatching, so only Gamma is left in the local doubt wrapper.

The final sentence reads donc and ends son tour. The preceding compact accent/dot form is retained as an uncertainty between à and a colon. The crossed que remains doubtful. The sentence is unfinished at the page edge and no terminal punctuation has been supplied.

All inventory kinds are restricted to text, display, diagram, drawing, margin note, insertion and deletion. Inserted and cancelled states are separate inventory entries where needed. All written numbers, including foliation and overwritten formula labels, are included in the blind-second-reading boxes.
No OCR, external sources, other page packet or TeX compilation was used. No theorem, lemma or claimed extension property was independently checked.

Main reader inspected the original and all eleven crops. The unclosed (118 label, absence of the terminal comma in the next display, retained underwritten digit doubts, local hooked-endpoint uncertainty, and the final donc / à-or-colon decisions were accepted. The editorial word stroke was removed from the arrow alternative before approval; only symbol alternatives remain in the transcription.

Blind audit confirms the live rewritten numbers 119 and 120 while retaining uncertainty in the old figures beneath them. The square’s upper label remains gamma, based on its two arms and descending loop. The final two-mark form now prefers colon tentatively over accented a; son tour is retained literally.
